questions.prompt: A rectangle has perimeter 36 m. If x is one side length, which one-variable objective and feasible domain model maximizing its nonzero area?
questions.explanation: The constraint is 2x+2y=36, so y=18−x. Substitute into area xy to get A=x(18−x). A nondegenerate rectangle requires x>0 and y>0, giving 0<x<18. The objective must describe area rather than the fixed constraint. A: This omits the factor 2 in the perimeter relation. B: The fixed perimeter is not the second side length. C: The other side is 18−x from 2x+2y=36, and both sides must be positive. D: This is the fixed perimeter, not the area objective.

questions.prompt: A rectangular pen lies against a straight river, so only its other three sides need a total of 60 m of fencing. If x is each perpendicular side, which area model is correct?
questions.explanation: Let y be the side parallel to the river that needs fencing. The constraint is 2x+y=60, giving y=60−2x. Thus area is x(60−2x). Both dimensions must be positive, so 0<x<30. A: This counts only one of the two perpendicular sides. B: This incorrectly treats all four sides as fenced. C: This is the remaining side length, not the area. D: Two perpendicular sides use 2x of fence, leaving 60−2x for the parallel side.

questions.prompt: Squares of side x cm are cut from each corner of a 20 cm square sheet, then sides are folded to form an open box. Which volume model and nondegenerate domain are correct?
questions.explanation: After cutting, the base is (20−2x) by (20−2x) and the height is x. Multiply these to get V=x(20−2x)². Nonzero height and positive base require x>0 and 20−2x>0, giving 0<x<10. A: The height is x and each base dimension loses two cuts. B: Each base dimension loses two x-length pieces, not one. C: The height is x, not the remaining base side. D: Positive height alone does not keep the base dimensions positive.

questions.prompt: A closed cylinder must have volume 54π cm³. Which function of radius r>0 should be minimized to minimize total surface area?
questions.explanation: The volume relation πr²h=54π gives h=54/r². A closed cylinder has area 2πr²+2πrh. Substitution gives S=2πr²+108π/r for positive radius; the corresponding height is also positive. A: A closed cylinder has two circular caps, not one. B: The volume constraint gives h=54/r², substituted into two caps plus lateral area. C: The height substitution leaves a reciprocal radius in the lateral term. D: This is the fixed volume rather than a surface-area objective.

questions.prompt: Positive numbers u and v satisfy u+v=12. Which one-variable function models minimizing u²+v²?
questions.explanation: Solve the constraint as v=12−u, then substitute into the requested sum of squares. The objective is u²+(12−u)². Positivity of both numbers requires u>0 and 12−u>0, giving the stated interval. A: This drops the square of v. B: This uses the wrong sign when solving the constraint. C: Use the sum constraint to eliminate v and keep both original squares. D: This is the fixed sum, not the sum of squares objective.

questions.prompt: A point (x,x²) on a parabola is to be chosen closest to (0,3). Which objective can be minimized without taking a square root?
questions.explanation: The horizontal difference is x−0=x and vertical difference is x²−3. Squaring and adding gives D²=x²+(x²−3)². Since the square-root function is increasing on nonnegative inputs, minimizing squared distance and distance selects the same point or points. A: This uses x rather than the point’s vertical coordinate x². B: The vertical difference from height 3 is x²−3. C: Vertical separation alone omits the horizontal distance. D: Squared Euclidean distance has the same minimizing inputs as distance.

questions.prompt: A continuous revenue model is R(q)=q(40−0.5q) dollars for 0≤q≤80 items. At which q is revenue maximized?
questions.explanation: Differentiate R=40q−0.5q² to get R′=40−q. The interior critical input is 40, where the second derivative is −1. Both endpoint values are zero while R(40)=800, so the maximum occurs at q=40. A: The derivative 40−q vanishes at 40 and the concave quadratic has zero endpoint revenues. B: This is the greatest allowed quantity, but the price and revenue are zero there. C: The revenue derivative is still positive there. D: This yields zero revenue, not its maximum.

questions.prompt: On the feasible interval 0≤x≤4, what input maximizes P(x)=20−(x−6)²?
questions.explanation: The derivative is −2(x−6)>0 for every x in [0,4]. The unrestricted stationary input 6 is infeasible. Compare the allowed endpoints: P(0)=−16 and P(4)=16, so the feasible maximum occurs at x=4. A: This unrestricted critical input is outside the feasible domain. B: The function is increasing throughout the feasible interval, so its right endpoint wins. C: This endpoint is farther from the parabola’s vertex and gives a lower value. D: This midpoint is not stationary and has a lower value than 4.

questions.prompt: A 30 m wire is divided between a circle of radius r and a square of side s. If the goal is to maximize their combined area, which pair correctly identifies constraint and objective?
questions.explanation: The circumference of the circle and perimeter of the square consume the wire: 2πr+4s=30. The combined enclosed area is A=πr²+s². These are different mathematical roles and have different dimensions. A: This exchanges area and length and mismatches their units. B: The square uses four side lengths of wire. C: Lengths add to the fixed wire total, while the two enclosed areas add in the objective. D: The proposed objective has length terms rather than the two areas.

questions.prompt: After finding an input where an objective derivative is zero, what must still be checked before claiming the constrained optimum?
options: Nothing; every derivative zero is automatically the requested optimum.
Only whether the input is positive, regardless of the other constraints.
Only whether the function value is zero.
Feasibility and the relevant extrema/endpoints or end behavior, then the requested output quantity.
questions.explanation: A correct optimization solution checks that the input satisfies every constraint, classifies or compares candidates, includes feasible endpoints or appropriate unbounded-domain behavior, and reports the quantity actually requested. The derivative equation supplies candidates, not a completed argument. A: Stationary inputs can be minima, maxima or neither. B: The feasible set can impose additional bounds and relations. C: The height zero has no general relation to optimality. D: A stationary input alone may be outside the domain or may not be the desired maximum or minimum.

questions.prompt: A point lies 3 m perpendicularly from a straight road. Its destination is on the road 10 m from the nearest road point. An off-road path ends x m along the road toward the destination, 0≤x≤10. Off-road travel costs 2 dollars/m and road travel 1 dollar/m. Which cost should be minimized?
questions.explanation: The off-road leg has perpendicular components 3 and x, so its length is √(9+x²). Multiply by the off-road cost 2. The road segment remaining has length 10−x and unit cost 1, giving C=2√(9+x²)+10−x on the stated feasible interval. A: Pythagoras gives the off-road distance, and the remaining road distance is 10−x. B: This uses a square root without squaring the perpendicular lengths. C: This incorrectly applies the off-road unit cost to the road segment too. D: The road distance remaining decreases rather than increases with x.
